actions.name: Conduct phishing campaigns to steal login credentials
actions.description: Malicious actors conduct phishing campaigns to steal login credentials for initial network access.

actions.name: Conduct phishing campaigns to deploy malware
actions.description: Malicious actors commonly conduct phishing campaigns to deploy malware for follow-on activity, such as interrupting or damaging systems, escalating user privileges, and maintaining persistence on compromised systems.

actions.name: Impersonate supervisors, trusted colleagues, or IT personnel to send targeted emails to deceive employees into providing their login credentials
actions.description: To obtain login credentials, malicious actors commonly impersonate supervisors, trusted colleagues, or IT personnel to send targeted emails to deceive employees into providing their login credentials.

actions.name: Use smartphones or tablets with SMS or chat platforms to lure users into divulging login credentials
actions.description: Malicious actors use smartphones or tablets, along with SMS, to send text messages or chats in platforms such as Slack, Teams, Signal, WhatsApp, or Facebook Messenger to lure users into divulging their login credentials.

actions.name: Use VoIP to spoof caller ID to deceive victims
actions.description: Malicious actors use voice over internet protocol (VoIP) to easily spoof caller identification (ID) which takes advantage of public trust in the security of phone services, especially landline phones.

actions.name: Exploit weak MFA implementations to gain access using compromised credentials
actions.description: Malicious actors can still obtain access through phishing and other techniques if weak forms of MFA are enabled, such as MFA without FIDO or PKI, push-notification MFA without number matching, or SMS/voice MFA.

actions.name: Send malicious hyperlinks or attachments to execute malware on host systems
actions.description: Malicious actors send malicious hyperlinks or attachments that cause a user to download malware, facilitating initial access, information stealing, damage or disruption to systems or services, and/or the escalation of account privileges.

actions.name: Use free publicly available tools to facilitate spearphishing campaigns
actions.description: Malicious actors may use free, publicly available tools (such as GoPhish or Zphisher) to facilitate spearphishing campaigns where individual users are targeted with specific and convincing lures.

actions.name: Send malicious attachments with macro scripts or obfuscated links that download malicious executables
actions.description: Malicious actors may send malicious attachments with macro scripts or messages with seemingly benign or obfuscated links that download malicious executables.

actions.name: Use smartphones or tablets with SMS or chat platforms to lure users into interacting with malicious hyperlinks or attachments that execute malware
actions.description: Malicious actors use smartphone or tablet apps, along with SMS, to send text messages or chats in collaboration platforms (i.e., Slack, Teams, Signal, WhatsApp, iMessage, and Facebook Messenger) to lure users into interacting with a malicious hyperlink or attachment that executes malware.
